wbc.name: White Blood Cell Count (WBC)
wbc.analogy: The security guards of your body that fight off infections and illnesses.
wbc.summary: WBCs are key components of your immune system. They increase when your body is fighting a cold, bacterial infection, or physical stress, and can decrease with certain viral illnesses or medications.
wbc.lifestyle_factors: Recent viral infection, intense exercise, emotional stress, corticosteroid medications, or smoking.
questions_for_doctor: Could my recent cold or stress explain this WBC count?
Do you recommend repeating this test in a few weeks to monitor the trend?
Are there any other signs or symptoms I should watch for?

rbc.name: Red Blood Cell Count (RBC)
rbc.analogy: The delivery trucks carrying oxygen from your lungs to every organ in your body.
rbc.summary: RBCs contain hemoglobin, which binds oxygen. Low levels can leave you feeling fatigued or short of breath, while high levels can be related to dehydration or living at high altitudes.
rbc.lifestyle_factors: Dehydration, high altitude living, heavy endurance training, or smoking.
questions_for_doctor: Does this RBC level relate to my overall energy and iron levels?
Could mild dehydration have affected this test result?

hemoglobin.name: Hemoglobin (Hgb)
hemoglobin.analogy: The oxygen-holding protein inside red blood cells.
hemoglobin.summary: Hemoglobin is the iron-rich protein that grabs oxygen in your lungs and releases it in your tissues. Lower levels are often seen in anemia.
hemoglobin.lifestyle_factors: Dietary iron intake, menstrual blood loss, pregnancy, or heavy exercise.
questions_for_doctor: Should I have my iron or ferritin levels checked based on this?
Are dietary changes appropriate before considering supplements?

hematocrit.name: Hematocrit (Hct)
hematocrit.analogy: The percentage of your total blood volume that consists of red blood cells.
hematocrit.summary: Hematocrit shows how thick or concentrated your blood is with red blood cells. Dehydration often causes a temporary increase.
hematocrit.lifestyle_factors: Fluid intake before the blood draw, sweating, or altitude.
questions_for_doctor: Was this result impacted by how much water I drank prior to the test?
How does this result compare with my previous blood tests?

platelets.name: Platelet Count (PLT)
platelets.analogy: The tiny bandage makers that form clots to stop cuts from bleeding.
platelets.summary: Platelets are cell fragments essential for normal blood clotting. Low levels can lead to easy bruising, while elevated levels often reflect temporary inflammation.
platelets.lifestyle_factors: Recent physical recovery, mild infection, aspirin, or anti-inflammatory medications.
questions_for_doctor: Could my current medications or over-the-counter pain relievers influence platelet counts?
Should I watch for unusual bruising or bleeding?

cholesterol_total.name: Total Cholesterol
cholesterol_total.analogy: The overall measurement of all waxy lipid fats circulating in your bloodstream.
cholesterol_total.summary: Total cholesterol combines HDL ('good'), LDL ('bad'), and other lipid components. It provides a baseline view of cardiovascular lipid balance.
cholesterol_total.lifestyle_factors: Dietary saturated fats, aerobic exercise frequency, genetics, and metabolic rate.
questions_for_doctor: What is my overall cardiovascular risk calculation rather than total cholesterol alone?
What specific dietary and exercise modifications would you recommend first?

cholesterol_ldl.name: LDL Cholesterol ('Bad')
cholesterol_ldl.analogy: The slow-moving delivery trucks that can leave excess cargo behind on blood vessel walls.
cholesterol_ldl.summary: Low-Density Lipoprotein (LDL) can build up inside artery walls over time if elevated. Lower numbers are generally desirable for arterial health.
cholesterol_ldl.lifestyle_factors: Diet high in saturated/trans fats, sedentary lifestyle, genetic family traits.
questions_for_doctor: Given my personal and family history, what is my ideal target for LDL?
How long should I try lifestyle changes before considering medication?

cholesterol_hdl.name: HDL Cholesterol ('Good')
cholesterol_hdl.analogy: The street sweepers that collect excess cholesterol and return it to the liver for disposal.
cholesterol_hdl.summary: High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL) helps protect cardiovascular health by clearing excess cholesterol. Higher numbers are generally protective.
cholesterol_hdl.lifestyle_factors: Regular aerobic exercise, olive oil/healthy fats, smoking cessation, and moderate weight.
questions_for_doctor: What specific exercises are most effective at boosting HDL levels?
Does my ratio of HDL to total cholesterol look reassuring?

triglycerides.name: Triglycerides
triglycerides.analogy: Stored energy fat droplets floating in the blood after meals.
triglycerides.summary: Triglycerides are the most common type of fat in the body, derived from calories not immediately used for energy. High levels often correlate with refined carb or alcohol intake.
triglycerides.lifestyle_factors: Fasting status (fasting vs non-fasting), alcohol consumption within 48 hours, sugar and refined carb intake.
questions_for_doctor: Did my fasting duration before the test affect this number?
What dietary adjustments have the greatest impact on lowering triglycerides?

glucose_fasting.name: Fasting Blood Glucose
glucose_fasting.analogy: The instant fuel level of sugar available in your blood tank right now.
glucose_fasting.summary: Fasting glucose measures your blood sugar after at least 8 hours without food. It assesses how effectively your body's insulin manages energy.
glucose_fasting.lifestyle_factors: Exact hours fasted, poor sleep the night before, acute stress, morning caffeine.
questions_for_doctor: How long was my fasting window, and does that contextualize this number?
Would an HbA1c test be helpful to see my 3-month average?

hba1c.name: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)
hba1c.analogy: A 90-day video of your blood sugar trends, rather than a single snapshot.
hba1c.summary: HbA1c reflects the percentage of hemoglobin coated with sugar over the 2-3 month lifespan of red blood cells. 5.7% to 6.4% indicates prediabetes range.
hba1c.lifestyle_factors: Long-term carbohydrate balance, consistency of physical activity, sleep regularity.
questions_for_doctor: What is our realistic target for my HbA1c over the next 6 months?
Can a consultation with a registered dietitian or diabetes educator be scheduled?

creatinine.name: Serum Creatinine
creatinine.analogy: The natural exhaust byproduct from muscle activity that healthy kidneys filter out.
creatinine.summary: Creatinine is a waste product filtered out by the kidneys. Elevated levels can indicate reduced kidney filtration efficiency or simple dehydration and high muscle mass.
creatinine.lifestyle_factors: Recent intense strength training, creatine supplements, dehydration, high red meat intake.
questions_for_doctor: Could my workout routine or hydration level have influenced this creatinine result?
What was my calculated eGFR (estimated filtration rate)?

bun.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
bun.analogy: Waste byproduct from breaking down protein, cleared by the kidneys.
bun.summary: BUN evaluates kidney and liver function. High levels often reflect mild dehydration or very high protein intake.
bun.lifestyle_factors: Low fluid intake, high-protein diet, strenuous physical exertion.
questions_for_doctor: How does the ratio between my BUN and creatinine look?
Should I increase my daily water intake before re-testing?

alt.name: Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT)
alt.analogy: An enzyme primarily found in liver cells that leaks into blood when liver cells are irritated.
alt.summary: ALT is a sensitive marker for liver health. Temporary elevations can occur from over-the-counter pain relievers (like acetaminophen), strenuous lifting, or alcohol.
alt.lifestyle_factors: Alcohol intake, acetaminophen or NSAID use, recent vigorous weight training.
questions_for_doctor: Could any medications or supplements I take be causing this liver enzyme fluctuation?
Do you recommend checking this again in 4 to 8 weeks?

tsh.name: Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH)
tsh.analogy: The thermostat signal from your brain telling your thyroid furnace how hard to burn.
tsh.summary: TSH is produced by the pituitary gland. When your thyroid is sluggish, TSH rises to signal it to work harder; when overactive, TSH drops.
tsh.lifestyle_factors: Time of blood draw (circadian rhythm), severe illness recovery, biotin supplements.
questions_for_doctor: Did I take biotin or any supplements that could interfere with this thyroid assay?
Would checking Free T4 and Free T3 give us a clearer overall picture?

vitamin_d.name: 25-Hydroxy Vitamin D
vitamin_d.analogy: The sunshine hormone critical for strong bones, immunity, and energy.
vitamin_d.summary: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption, bone density, and immune balance. Many people have suboptimal levels during winter or indoor work.
vitamin_d.lifestyle_factors: Sunlight exposure, skin pigmentation, sunscreen usage, geographical latitude.
questions_for_doctor: What daily or weekly vitamin D3 dosage is appropriate for my target level?
When should we recheck my levels after supplementation?
